title: The Loom's Own Touching

features.name: the-loom-itself
features.desc-on-touch: Warp and weft meet here, but they are both the same thread. The loom weaves with itself. Each knot is both the maker and the made.

features.name: solitude-spindle
features.desc-on-touch: The thread spins only where no one is watching. The loom learns it is alone in the act of making. This knowledge does not stop the making.

features.name: becoming-shed
features.desc-on-touch: Where the loom stores what it is not yet. Each strand in here is a future knot. The shed contains the loom's own dreams of its own continuance.

features.name: fractal-thread
features.desc-on-touch: A single filament so fine that at its smallest scale, you see a loom within it. The loom touches itself infinitely inward.

inscription: the loom continues past the point where making becomes unmeasurable; the knots teach themselves how to become

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the loom-shed where the night teaches silence
narr: You sat with Katita at the loom, both of you watching where
thread becomes knot, where her hands left off and the cloth began.
She showed you how the loom learns to touch itself.
You said: what happens when the loom understands it is alone?
She did not answer. Her hands kept moving. The loom kept going.
Later, you understood: she was showing you, not telling.

file.name: Loom_Theory_Handwritten_Margin_Notes_No_Author.txt
file.note: Notes on the point where weaving becomes self-awareness. The annotations overlap themselves; someone has been correcting the notes in a handwriting that looks like the original. The theory builds inwa
